audit.why: Difficulty HARD 8/10 is consistent with Sylas being a mobile, sustaining diver against an immobile mage; win rate 51.1% over 3552 games is near-even, so the lane is playable but skill-gated on the Q root.

Spikes on the page match the kits: Lux's Final Spark at 6 (60/50/40s), Luden's first item, and Sylas's Hijack at 6 (80/55/30s) plus Kingslayer scaling (12/10.5/9/7.5/6s) are all real. Sylas's Abscond drops from 13s to 9s across ranks, which is the real mid-lane spike for him.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no cooldown number at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and enemyWin was a name-swap template that never stated the actual Abscond -> Abduct recast mechanic.
audit.why: Abscond (E) is a 400-range dash on 13/12/11/10/9s that can be RECAST as Abduct to chain-pull onto a champion it hits. The pull only exists while the dash is spent, so the dash going down is the green light. Kingslayer (W, 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s, 400 range) heals him against champions, which is why chip poke alone does not win extended trades.
audit.corrected: cooldowns field now names Abscond/Abduct 13s->9s, Kingslayer 12s, and Prismatic Barrier 12s; enemyWin now states the dash-recast-heal sequence.

audit.whatIsWrong: The trading/mid text never told the player to buy Grievous Wounds against Kingslayer.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal: Kingslayer heals Sylas against champions, so anti-heal timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: breakdown.mid now names Oblivion Orb and the Grievous Wounds requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT: the cooldowns field carried no cooldown number.
audit.why: An earlier proposal targeted these same fields but its replacement text overshot the +/-10% length rule, so apply-proposals dropped the edit and the defect survived on disk.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the same meaning inside the length budget, grounded in real ability names and cooldowns from champ-data/_kits: breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Abscond/Abduct: 13s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — his dash into chain-stun; punish him hard while it is down. - Prismatic Barrier is 12s and spending it on poke is a death you scheduled. - Final Spark is 60s: hold it for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Sylas wins by dashing Abscond in, recasting Abduct to chain onto you, then healing the trade back with Kingslayer before your Q returns.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Abscond only reaches 400 units, so a wave held at centre keeps him outside it, and a warded flank removes the angle he needs to open on you.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Holding Lucent Singularity to detonate leaves you standing in Chain Lash range at half HP — pop it early and step back, not late.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by making Abscond a losing button: root the dash on arrival and laser him from 3340 range, never standing as the lone target in W range.

edits.before: Luden's onward, every root is a kill: shove, hover the river, and Q-R the first contest. Your range decides objective setups alone.
edits.after: Luden's onward every root is a kill, but grab Oblivion Orb early — Kingslayer heals him out of your chip without Grievous Wounds on him.
